subject.title: Support reasoning-field outputs and visible final-answer handling for native reasoning models

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic opt-in reasoning-to-final-answer and benchmark-reporting contract, or keep final-answer normalization provider-owned while limiting core to private reasoning ingestion and aggregate diagnostics?
rationale: The choice affects chain-of-thought privacy, provider ownership, configuration surface, tool/JSON safety, and whether raw reasoning may be stored or displayed; source inspection cannot determine the intended product policy.

options.title: Provider-owned normalization
options.body: Keep core reasoning private, add provider hooks for visible-output enforcement or narrowly approved final promotion, and expose only aggregate compatibility diagnostics by default.

options.title: Generic opt-in extraction
options.body: Add a core model/profile mode that may promote reasoning into final output, with explicit redaction, persistence, channel, tool, and JSON-task restrictions.

options.title: Reporting-only scope
options.body: Implement compatibility counters and extraction-source reporting first, leaving runtime reasoning-only answers unsupported until a later policy decision.

recommendation.title: Provider-owned normalization
recommendation.body: Keep core reasoning private, add provider hooks for visible-output enforcement or narrowly approved final promotion, and expose only aggregate compatibility diagnostics by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans repository-wide provider ownership, security posture, and configuration policy rather than a mechanical parser fix.
